findings.title: No submit button visible inside the login card
findings.description: The acceptance criterion requires the login form's submit button to be fully visible inside the card and viewport. In the rendered card (roughly x=64..736, y=45..383) the visible sequence is the "Login" heading, the "Email" label with its field, and the "Password" label with its field. Below the password field the card interior from about y=295 to the card's bottom border at y=383 is unmasked plain white with no button, label, or control of any kind, and no submit control appears anywhere else in the 800x600 viewport. The region where a submit control would be expected is therefore visible and empty, so the criterion's required control cannot be confirmed as present on screen. Reported as a hypothesis about the visible pixels only; nothing here determines whether the element exists in the DOM, is positioned outside the captured viewport, or is otherwise not painted.
findings.suggestedCheck: In a browser at 800x600, load the login page and query the form's submit control (e.g. button[type=submit] / input[type=submit]). Assert exactly one exists, then read getBoundingClientRect() and assert width>0, height>0, and that top/left/bottom/right fall inside both the card element's rect and the viewport (0,0,800,600). Independently assert document.documentElement.scrollWidth <= clientWidth to confirm no horizontal scrolling is required to reach it.
